issues.failure_explanation: The infimum is zero only if the relevant conditional-expectation target is represented exactly by the chosen finite neural-network class. No such realizability hypothesis is imposed, and universal approximation does not imply exact representation by a fixed architecture. Thus a positive approximation error may remain even under exact optimization.

failure_location.quote: The accuracy of the DBR scheme can also be tested when computing at each time step the infimum of loss function, which should be equal to zero as the DBDP scheme in \cite{GMPHWX22}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the zero-infimum claim by a statement involving the best-in-class approximation error, or add an exact realizability assumption.
issues.overall_effect: Loss values cannot generally be interpreted as residuals that should approach zero, so the proposed accuracy diagnostic is unreliable.
issues.title: The claimed zero infimum of the DBR losses is not guaranteed
issues.why_classification: A local qualification preserves the method and all rate claims while withdrawing only the exact-zero diagnostic.

issues.failure_explanation: For a Brownian filtration, an arbitrary next-step random variable is not generally an affine function of the single increment \(\Delta W_i\). The conditional formulas determine its projection onto constants and \(\Delta W_i\), but the displayed pathwise equality additionally requires the orthogonal martingale residual to vanish. Consequently the two formulations are not equivalent as asserted.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the numerical scheme directly by the conditional equations, or add the missing orthogonal martingale-increment residual to each pathwise equation.
issues.overall_effect: The derivations that present the conditional scheme as a rewriting of an exact pathwise Euler difference equation are mathematically incorrect, including the analogous Monte Carlo and reflected formulations.
issues.title: The pathwise Euler BSDE equation is not equivalent to the conditional scheme
issues.why_classification: The conditional scheme itself remains usable after a standard local correction to the pathwise formulation.

issues.failure_explanation: The backward loop starts at \(i=N-1\), but only \(X_0\) is initialized, so \(X_{N-1}^{\pi,m}\) and the other required forward states have not been generated. Moreover, the next-time network is evaluated with \(\theta^*_{y,i}\) rather than its own already-trained parameter \(\theta^*_{y,i+1}\). Finally, \(X_i^{\pi,m,k}\) is used for \(\mathcal Z_i^{m,k}\) and in the Y loss although only \(X_{i+1}^{\pi,m,k}\) was generated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Precompute complete forward paths before the backward loop, use the already-trained parameter \(\theta^*_{y,i+1}\) for the next-time network, and consistently evaluate the time-\(i\) generator and Z network at the defined parent state \(X_i^{\pi,m}\).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised fully implementable algorithm is not executable as written and does not unambiguously implement the preceding DBR recursion.
issues.title: Algorithm 1 uses undefined and incorrectly indexed states and parameters
issues.why_classification: The intended architecture is recognizable, but repairing several coupled state and parameter indices is necessary to obtain a well-defined procedure.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\mu$ and $\sigma$ are Lipschitz continuous of the spatial variable $x$;

issues.failure_explanation: Spatial Lipschitz continuity alone does not imply convergence of the left-point Euler approximation when the coefficients may be arbitrarily irregular in time. For example, with deterministic drift \(\mu(t,x)=1_{\mathbb Q}(t)\), \(\sigma=0\), rational grid points, \(f(t,x,y,z)=x\), and \(g=0\), the exact forward process is constant while the Euler process accumulates drift \(h\) at every step. The resulting discrete backward values have an order-one error although the theorem's displayed right-hand side can be order \(h\). Thus the quoted forward estimate and the theorem fail under the stated assumptions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add sufficient temporal regularity or an explicit Euler-consistency condition for \(\mu\) and \(\sigma\), and propagate it through the forward and backward discretization estimates.
issues.overall_effect: The DBR error theorem and both convergence results are unsupported for the time-irregular coefficients allowed by assumptions (i)-(iv).
issues.title: The forward Euler estimate is used without temporal regularity of the coefficients
issues.why_classification: A standard additional coefficient-regularity hypothesis restores the intended discretization regime without changing the method or rate.

issues.failure_explanation: The preceding estimate for the second term contains an order-one constant arising from the variance of the finite-path target, but the next displayed bound removes it without justification. More fundamentally, the difference between a finite Monte Carlo average and its conditional expectation is a current-step sampling error; it is not controlled by the listed next-step residuals. At the terminal backward step this sampling error can be nonzero even when the fitted empirical residual is zero. The proof therefore does not establish the residual-only error bound, and its use of \(R_{i+1,*}\) at \(i=N-1\) also refers to residuals not defined in the construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must retain and quantitatively control every current-step Monte Carlo fluctuation, define the terminal-index residuals, and redo the backward stability argument with those terms.
issues.overall_effect: The central DBR upper error bound, the convergence theorem built from it, and the reflected proof that invokes the same Steps 2–4 are unreliable.
issues.title: Theorem 3.1 drops a nonzero Monte Carlo variance term
issues.why_classification: The missing stochastic-error control is central to the claimed bound and requires a replacement error analysis rather than a local algebraic correction.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds population best-in-class approximation errors, but the DBR method uses minimizers of finite empirical losses with recursively estimated targets. No generalization bound, optimization error bound, stability argument, or condition on the outer sample size \(M\) relates those empirical minimizers to the displayed population infima. Hence the derived GroupSort approximation bounds do not imply the asserted error rate for the trained networks.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: f(t, x, y, z)=\hat{k}(t, x)-\frac{y}{\sqrt{d}}\left(1_d \cdot z\right)-\frac{y^2}{2},
\partial_t u + \frac{1}{2} \operatorname{Tr}\left(\frac{I_d}{\sqrt{d}} (\frac{I_d}{\sqrt{d}})^{\top} D_x^2 u\right)=f\left(\cdot, \cdot, u, \sigma^{\top} D_x u\right)

issues.failure_explanation: The index \(i\) in \(D_{x_i}u\) is free, so \(\hat k\) is not defined as a scalar function. Moreover, because \(z=\sigma^\top D_xu=D_xu/\sqrt d\), cancellation in the PDE requires the term \((u/d)\sum_iD_{x_i}u\), not \((u/\sqrt d)D_{x_i}u\). Thus the displayed forcing does not make the subsequently stated function a solution.

failure_location.quote: with $\hat{k}(t, x)=\partial_t u+\frac{1}{2 d} \operatorname{Tr}\left(D_x^2 u\right)+\frac{u}{\sqrt{d}} D_{x_i} u+\frac{u^2}{2}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine \(\hat k\) with the correctly summed and scaled gradient term, then verify that the implementation and all reported reference values used that corrected PDE.
issues.overall_effect: The second numerical benchmark is mathematically undefined as written, so its claimed exact solution, errors, and validation conclusions do not correspond to the displayed PDE.
